Senses.Explanation: Chang’an’s great road is the broad, direct road to the capital. The records place it among monastery approaches, in case-verses, and in direct questions about where the road is met. Yangshan Qingjian says the pines lining the way go straight through to Chang’an’s road. Dawei Fabao’s Bodhidharma verse calls it straight as a string; Miyin Zhenchuan answers that one steps on it upon leaving the gate; Panshan Langkong Shun calls it level and open.
